critiquedBy: @qa protocol review, orchestrated by @aiox-master; no independent reviewer claimed
verdictReason: Refreshed requirements cover every accepted field, privacy boundary, capability lifecycle, OBS permissions and TLS constraint. Current code readiness and upstream status are documented. Remaining native CEF trust and performance checks are explicit implementation/compatibility gates, not unresolved product-policy decisions.

observations.description: The exact native OBS CEF trust path for the app's local CA is not known and has not been tested. No OS/OBS compatibility can be claimed until the target installation passes the HTTPS preflight.
observations.mitigation: Use the existing local HTTPS health endpoint in native Browser Source and record OS/OBS/CEF versions. Keep TLS validation on and fail closed if trust fails. This is an implementation gate and does not block UX planning.

observations.description: The eight-page two-second target and OBS rendering/resource cost still require measured real-app and native OBS acceptance.
observations.mitigation: Measure ten consecutive commit-to-DOM changes with eight active/enabled pages, then record native OBS performance and environment; do not report completion without evidence.

resolvedFindings: FND-5 and FND-6 status corrected to complete and merged in PR #16/#22; code-level readiness mapping recorded.
Called-viewer position uses persisted audit previousPosition because active entry position is cleared; multi-call selection is deterministic by calledAt then createdAt.
OBS Browser Source least privilege is explicit: Page Permissions=None and no OBS bindings/control APIs.
Local HTTPS certificate validation is mandatory; no HTTP fallback or bypass, with native CEF preflight added before renderer work.
Two-second SLA is scoped to active/enabled pages; hidden unloaded sources fetch current data when resumed.
FND-7 JSON/YAML plans align on 24 tasks; bilingual story and validation documents reflect the same criteria.
securityNote: Widget URLs remain bearer capabilities even with the secret in the URL fragment. Keep one-time issuance, hash-only persistence, no-store/no-referrer headers, scoped projections, and immediate revocation. The broad existing queue projection contains conditionally visible UID and must never be returned to OBS as-is.
nextAction: Proceed to @aiox-ux-design-expert refinement. Do not begin UI implementation until UX decisions are recorded and implementation-time FND-5/FND-6/readiness and native HTTPS CEF gates pass.
limitations: This is a planning critique, not QA of implementation. No FND-7 code, tests, OBS installation, TLS compatibility, resource usage, or operating-system support was validated.
